testcase: CREATE KNOWLEDGE against an explicit bucket.scope.collection succeeds for an admin user
statements: CREATE KNOWLEDGE icao_hint FOR orders.knowledge_test.articles AS "ICAO codes represent airports."

testcase: the new entry shows up in system:natural_knowledge - fetched directly by its composite key (USE KEYS) rather than via a keyspace/name predicate, so this doesn't depend on GSI index catch-up for the just-written doc
statements: SELECT `name`, `value`, `keyspace` FROM system:natural_knowledge WHERE `keyspace` = "default:orders.knowledge_test.articles"

testcase: creating a second, differently named, entry for the same keyspace succeeds
statements: CREATE KNOWLEDGE iata_hint FOR orders.knowledge_test.articles AS "IATA codes are the 3-letter airport identifiers used by airlines."

testcase: both entries are now visible for that keyspace
statements: SELECT `name` FROM system:natural_knowledge WHERE `keyspace` = "default:orders.knowledge_test.articles" ORDER BY `name`

testcase: re-creating a knowledge entry with a name already used for that keyspace fails
statements: CREATE KNOWLEDGE icao_hint FOR orders.knowledge_test.articles AS "a different hint"

testcase: the same name is still usable for a different keyspace
statements: CREATE KNOWLEDGE icao_hint FOR orders.knowledge_test.flights AS "flights-specific hint"

testcase: AS accepts a named parameter, resolved against the request's arguments
statements: CREATE KNOWLEDGE named_param_hint FOR orders.knowledge_test.flights AS $hint

namedArgs.hint: hint supplied via a named parameter

testcase: the named-parameter value was evaluated and stored, not the parameter itself - USE KEYS again, for the same reason as above
statements: SELECT `value` FROM system:natural_knowledge USE KEYS "default:orders.knowledge_test.flights::named_param_hint"

results.value: hint supplied via a named parameter

testcase: USE KEYS on system:natural_knowledge does not leak entries for a bucket the requesting user has no access to - reviewowner has no privileges on the orders bucket, so the fetch must be filtered out even though the key itself exists
statements: SELECT `value` FROM system:natural_knowledge USE KEYS "default:orders.knowledge_test.flights::named_param_hint"

testcase: AS accepts a positional parameter, resolved against the request's arguments
statements: CREATE KNOWLEDGE positional_param_hint FOR orders.knowledge_test.flights AS $1
positionalArgs: hint supplied via a positional parameter

testcase: a non-admin user is not allowed to create knowledge
statements: CREATE KNOWLEDGE not_allowed FOR orders.knowledge_test.articles AS "should not be created"
error: User does not have credentials to run this type of query. Add role admin to allow the statement to run.

testcase: CREATE KNOWLEDGE against a non-existent scope fails
statements: CREATE KNOWLEDGE missing_scope_hint FOR orders.nosuchscope.nosuchcoll AS "should not be created"
error: Scope not found in CB datastore default:orders.nosuchscope

testcase: CREATE KNOWLEDGE against the bucket-local _system scope is rejected, mirroring CREATE SEQUENCE's rejection of the same reserved scope
statements: CREATE KNOWLEDGE system_scope_hint FOR orders._system._query AS "should not be created"

testcase: the rejected system-scope entry above was not created - FROM's bulk form is rejected the same way
statements: CREATE KNOWLEDGE FOR orders._system._query FROM {"a": "should not be created"}

testcase: AS is syntactically a general expression, but semantics rejects anything that isn't a string constant or a named/positional parameter
statements: CREATE KNOWLEDGE non_string_value_hint FOR orders.knowledge_test.articles AS 123
error: Invalid knowledge data: value must be a string, not number

testcase: a named parameter resolving to a non-string value is rejected at execution time
statements: CREATE KNOWLEDGE bad_named_param_hint FOR orders.knowledge_test.articles AS $hint
error: Invalid knowledge data: value must be a string, not number

testcase: CREATE KNOWLEDGE FOR ... FROM <object> creates multiple entries for a keyspace in a single statement
statements: CREATE KNOWLEDGE FOR orders.knowledge_test.articles FROM {"bulk_a": "First bulk hint", "bulk_b": "Second bulk hint"}

testcase: both bulk-created entries are visible alongside the earlier AS-created ones
statements: SELECT `name` FROM system:natural_knowledge WHERE `keyspace` = "default:orders.knowledge_test.articles" ORDER BY `name`

testcase: CREATE KNOWLEDGE FOR ... FROM <object> fails entirely if any one of the object's names already exists for that keyspace - icao_hint is a duplicate here, so bulk_c (which isn't) must not be added either
statements: CREATE KNOWLEDGE FOR orders.knowledge_test.articles FROM {"bulk_c": "should not be added", "icao_hint": "duplicate, should fail"}

testcase: the failed bulk create above was atomic - bulk_c was not added despite not itself being a duplicate
statements: SELECT `name` FROM system:natural_knowledge WHERE `keyspace` = "default:orders.knowledge_test.articles" ORDER BY `name`

testcase: CREATE OR REPLACE KNOWLEDGE overwrites an existing entry's value instead of failing with already-exists
statements: CREATE OR REPLACE KNOWLEDGE icao_hint FOR orders.knowledge_test.articles AS "Replaced ICAO hint"

testcase: the value was actually replaced - USE KEYS by the known composite key, same reasoning as the earlier read-after-write checks
statements: SELECT `value` FROM system:natural_knowledge USE KEYS "default:orders.knowledge_test.articles::icao_hint"

testcase: the replace did not create a duplicate entry - articles still has exactly the same 4 names as before
statements: SELECT `name` FROM system:natural_knowledge WHERE `keyspace` = "default:orders.knowledge_test.articles" ORDER BY `name`

testcase: CREATE OR REPLACE KNOWLEDGE without an explicit name is rejected - an auto-generated implicit name can never already exist, so REPLACE would be meaningless
statements: CREATE OR REPLACE KNOWLEDGE FOR orders.knowledge_test.articles AS "x"

testcase: a name is still not permitted together with FROM, with or without OR REPLACE
statements: CREATE OR REPLACE KNOWLEDGE some_name FOR orders.knowledge_test.articles FROM {"a": "b"}
error: a name is not permitted with FROM

testcase: CREATE OR REPLACE KNOWLEDGE FOR ... FROM <object> replaces existing names and adds new ones in the same call
statements: CREATE OR REPLACE KNOWLEDGE FOR orders.knowledge_test.articles FROM {"icao_hint": "Bulk-replaced ICAO hint", "bulk_d": "New bulk entry"}

testcase: both effects of the bulk replace are visible - icao_hint's value changed, bulk_d was added, and no duplicates were created
statements: SELECT `name`, `value` FROM system:natural_knowledge WHERE `keyspace` = "default:orders.knowledge_test.articles" ORDER BY `name`

results.name: iata_hint
results.value: IATA codes are the 3-letter airport identifiers used by airlines.

testcase: system:natural_knowledge supports filtering by bucket via its secondary index
statements: SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM system:natural_knowledge WHERE `bucket` = "orders" AND `scope` = "knowledge_test"

testcase: CREATE OR REPLACE KNOWLEDGE succeeds against a scope and collection at Couchbase's 251-character name limit - exercises capKeySegment hashing both name segments down so the underlying document key stays well clear of the 251-byte KV key limit
statements: CREATE OR REPLACE KNOWLEDGE aa1 FOR orders.`aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`.`bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb` AS "blah-blah-blah-blah-BLAH"

testcase: the entry is readable back by its composite key despite the long names - USE KEYS, same reasoning as the earlier read-after-write checks
statements: SELECT `value` FROM system:natural_knowledge USE KEYS "default:orders.aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb::aa1"

testcase: a second entry for the same long-named keyspace also succeeds - exercises the read-modify-write path against the already-existing (hashed-key) document, not just its creation
statements: CREATE KNOWLEDGE aa2 FOR orders.`aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa`.`bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb` AS "second hint for the long-named keyspace"

testcase: both entries for the long-named keyspace are visible, and only those two - confirms the hashed key isn't colliding with anything else
statements: SELECT `name` FROM system:natural_knowledge WHERE `keyspace` = "default:orders.aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa.bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb" ORDER BY `name`
